response: Yes, patients in regional and rural settings are willing partners in developing the skills of junior medical students. In fact, studies have shown that patients in these areas are underutilized partners in community-based medical training, and their support could facilitate the expansion of primary care-based medical education in areas where there is a significant workforce need. Junior medical students in regional and rural settings have greater involvement in patient consultations than their urban counterparts, indicating a positive and willing participation from patients in the community-based medical education process.
